nodes.summary: If the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, then $a_j = \sum_{i} r_{ij}\, q_i$ for every $j$.
nodes.title: Each column is the combination of the Q columns with coefficients from R

nodes.summary: For a real $m \times k$ matrix $A$ and an index $j$, `colVec A j` is the $j$-th column $a_j = (A_{ij})_i$ of $A$, viewed as a vector of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^m$ with its standard inner product.
nodes.title: Column of a matrix as a Euclidean vector

nodes.summary: If $U$ and $V$ are upper triangular $k \times k$ real matrices, then $(UV)_{ii} = U_{ii} V_{ii}$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Diagonal of a product of upper triangular matrices

nodes.summary: If the columns of the real matrix $A$ are linearly independent, then $A = QR$ for the Gram–Schmidt factors $Q$ and $R$.
nodes.title: The Gram–Schmidt factors reproduce the matrix

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a real $m \times k$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent (full column rank, so $k \le m$). Then there are an $m \times k$ matrix $Q$ with orthonormal columns, $Q^{\mathsf{T}} Q = I_k$, and an upper triangular $k \times k$ matrix $R$ with positive diagonal entries such that $A = QR$.
nodes.title: Existence of the reduced QR factorization

nodes.summary: For every real $m \times k$ matrix $A$, the Gram–Schmidt factor $R$ is upper triangular: $r_{ij} = \langle q_i, a_j \rangle = 0$ for $i > j$, because $a_j$ lies in the span of $q_1, \dots, q_j$.
nodes.title: The Gram–Schmidt R factor is upper triangular

nodes.summary: For a real $m \times k$ matrix $A$ with columns $a_1, \dots, a_k$, `qrQ A` is the $m \times k$ matrix whose $j$-th column is $q_j = v_j / \|v_j\|$, the normalized $j$-th vector of the Gram–Schmidt process applied to $a_1, \dots, a_k$ (with the convention $q_j = 0$ when $v_j = 0$).
nodes.title: The Q factor of the Gram–Schmidt QR factorization

nodes.summary: If the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, then $r_{jj} = \|v_j\| > 0$ for every $j$, where $v_j$ is the $j$-th (unnormalized) Gram–Schmidt vector.
nodes.title: The Gram–Schmidt R factor has positive diagonal

nodes.summary: For a real $m \times k$ matrix $A$, `qrR A` is the $k \times k$ matrix with entries $r_{ij} = \langle q_i, a_j \rangle$, where $q_i$ is the $i$-th column of the Gram–Schmidt factor $Q$ and $a_j$ the $j$-th column of $A$.
nodes.title: The R factor of the Gram–Schmidt QR factorization

nodes.summary: Let $Q, Q'$ be real $m \times k$ matrices with $Q^{\mathsf{T}} Q = Q'^{\mathsf{T}} Q' = I_k$ and let $R, R'$ be upper triangular $k \times k$ matrices with positive diagonal entries. If $QR = Q'R'$, then $Q = Q'$ and $R = R'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the reduced QR factorization

nodes.summary: If the columns of the real $m \times k$ matrix $A$ are linearly independent, the Gram–Schmidt factor $Q$ satisfies $Q^{\mathsf{T}} Q = I_k$.
nodes.title: The Gram–Schmidt Q factor has orthonormal columns

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
